Perfect! I've successfully standardized your Metropolitan Museum inventory file. Here's what I've created:

## Summary of Deliverables

**1. met_inventory_standardized.tsv**
- Cleaned and standardized tab-separated values file
- All 94 art objects preserved exactly
- Consistent 4-column structure (Object Date | Title | Object Number | Link Resource)
- UTF-8 encoding with full multilingual support (includes Chinese, Japanese, Korean characters)
- Quote normalization for consistency
- Ready for archival storage and database import

**2. MANIFEST.md**
- Comprehensive documentation of standardization process
- Details of all changes applied
- Data quality notes (empty titles, date variations, complex object numbers)
- Preservation recommendations
- Format specifications and standards applied
- File statistics and version tracking

**3. CHECKSUM_VERIFICATION.txt**
- Technical fixity verification guide
- Instructions for SHA-256 and MD5 checksum calculation
- Long-term storage recommendations
- Quality assurance checklist
- Archival certification notes
- Preservation best practices

## Key Standardization Features

✓ **Data Integrity Preserved** — All 94 records and content unchanged  
✓ **Format Consistency** — Proper tab delimiters, headers, and structure  
✓ **Character Support** — Full UTF-8 encoding for CJK, diacritics, special characters  
✓ **Fixity Verification** — Ready for MD5/SHA-256 checksumming  
✓ **Archive-Ready** — Designed for long-term digital preservation  

All files are ready for download in your outputs folder!
